title: Caries risk assessment and management
section: Caries detection and diagnosis; ADA Caries Classification System
text: Caries assessment combines clinical findings, radiographic information and patient history. Bitewing radiographs can help detect proximal lesions, with performance depending on lesion stage. A panoramic detector candidate alone does not establish lesion activity, depth, or a patient's caries risk.
consideration: Correlate a caries candidate with clinical examination and appropriate diagnostic imaging; lesion activity and depth remain unassessed here.

title: Save a Tooth, Maybe Save a Life
section: Radiographic interpretation, pulp testing and differential diagnosis
text: Periapical radiolucencies can have endodontic and non-endodontic causes. Radiographic appearance alone cannot definitively establish the nature of a lesion. History, clinical examination and pulp testing provide context for a differential diagnosis.
consideration: Review a periapical candidate with clinical history, examination and pulp testing; the image alone does not establish pulpal disease.

title: Periodontitis: 2017 World Workshop consensus, published 2018
section: Table 1A: staging by severity, complexity, extent and distribution
text: Periodontitis staging uses clinical attachment loss, radiographic bone loss, periodontal tooth loss and complexity factors. Clinical attachment loss is the initial basis; radiographic bone loss may be used if it is unavailable. A complete classification requires more information than a panoramic image or a segmentation mask.
consideration: Periodontal staging is not provided by OrthoGraph; clinical measurements and case context are required.

title: Guidance on the extraction of wisdom teeth (TA1)
text: NICE guidance in the NHS context advises against prophylactic removal of pathology-free impacted third molars and restricts surgery to cases with evidence of pathology. Identifying a third molar on an image does not establish impaction, pathology, or an indication for extraction.
consideration: Review eruption status and clinical context. Third-molar detection alone does not justify extraction; NICE TA1 addresses this in the NHS setting.
